title: Full-Key Recovery for Reduced-Round AES-256
summary: The attacks on AES-256 variants with up to 10 rounds recover only some key bytes; extending each to full-key recovery at the same complexity remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For each attack presented against an $\mathrm{AES}\text{-}256$ variant with up to $10$ rounds, the established result recovers only some key bytes; extend each attack to full key recovery while staying within that attack's stated complexity.

scope.domain: Key-recovery cryptanalysis of AES-256 variants with up to 10 rounds.
parameters: Round count: at most 10 rounds in the targeted AES-256 variant
Attack complexity: each extension must remain within the corresponding attack's stated complexity
scope.unresolved_remainder: Extend every presented partial-key-recovery attack to recover the full key without exceeding that attack's stated complexity.

citations.label: Key Recovery Attacks of Practical Complexity on AES-256 Variants with up to 10 Rounds

progress.summary: The source summarizes the presented attacks as recovering only some key bytes and expresses the expectation that they can be extended to full-key recovery at the same complexity.
citation_labels: Alex Biryukov et al., Key Recovery Attacks of Practical Complexity on AES-256 Variants with up to 10 Rounds
